transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… work is what pushed me to come in. I’m an industrial production manager, so I’m used to juggling a lot, but lately I went from, like, launching nonstop plant redesign projects and calling suppliers after hours—probably way too much, honestly—and rewriting the whole shift plan by myself… to suddenly not being able to keep up with any of the plans I’d set in motion.

And it’s embarrassing, because at first it felt like I was finally fixing everything. I even had this whole idea about the packaging line layout—sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is I created this massive wave of work, and now I can’t keep up with it, and it’s starting to feel out of control.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially in relation to this recent change in your work performance?

Yeah… I think so. Lately I wake up in this temporary apartment I’m staying in, and there’s just this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I’ve even gotten in the car to drive to the plant.

And the apartment is awful, honestly—not awful like unsafe, just… temporary, beige walls, weird humming fridge, all my stuff still in boxes because I kept telling myself I’d only be there a little while. But I wake up and it’s like none of the work stuff even has to happen yet and I already feel sunk.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, don’t feel as rewarding or interesting lately?

I don’t know… maybe? I haven’t really been keeping track of that. I mean, I used to say yes to things more easily, like if someone invited me out, but lately everything feels kind of tied up in work and the apartment and just trying to get through the week.

I haven’t even unpacked my coffee grinder, which is stupid because I used to be weirdly into making coffee a certain way. But then I think, well, that’s not exactly a hobby, it’s just coffee, and then I start thinking about how I should’ve bought different shelves for the kitchen because the cabinets there make no sense. So… I’m not sure if it’s that things don’t feel rewarding, or I just haven’t really been doing much of anything.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high, you felt extremely energetic, or you were easily irritable for several days or longer?

Yeah… I think so. At the beginning of this assignment I felt almost, I don’t know, electrically upbeat? Like everything was suddenly obvious and I could see exactly how the plant should run.

And then it tipped into me getting weirdly irritated with people. If someone questioned one of my ideas, I’d feel like they were slowing down something that was clearly important. I remember thinking, why are we wasting time debating this, when the answer is right there? Which sounds harsh when I say it out loud.
Have you ever had a time when you felt so good or so irritable that people around you noticed a change in your behavior, or when you were doing things that were out of character for you?

Yeah… people definitely noticed. I mean, I didn’t think it was out of character at the time, I thought I was finally doing what needed to be done.

I came in and just started launching all these plant redesign projects nonstop—like one idea would turn into three, and then I’d be calling suppliers after hours because I was convinced we could move faster if everyone would just keep up. I rewrote the shift plan myself, too, which… looking back, was probably not normal. I remember being annoyed that it took so long to format, actually, because the spreadsheet kept doing this thing with the cells—sorry, that’s not the point.

The point is, I set all these plans in motion, and then later I suddenly couldn’t keep up with any of them. It was like I’d created this whole machine and then couldn’t run it. So yes, I think that was a change people could see.
